just use $? for single command status.

We should not copy the hook logic here. I am thinking that we set a v2 flag upon the successful download of metadata file. If the flag is true, we skip the v1 download process.

Then modify each hook to check this flag, if it is true, download the individual files they need, if not stay the same as today. This will give you the flexibility of adding customized logic in each hook (e.g. check version and skip download image if they are the same), while still reusing most of the code.
we should reuse the GBMC_UPGRADE_HOOK here

Probably we should re-order this json to put message earlier (first?)? We want it to be as human readable is possible on the serial console.

I'm thinking message -> state -> code -> time -> retries
I believe we need to be able to distinguish `ONGOING` vs `ERROR` and so we need a way to set the right bit in `update-dhcp-status` too.
Yes that work is not done yet and still being scoped, so for now we'll just go with that.
Why? that is exactly tied into this work. The logging function should handle all of the logging, not require multiple output statements to make this work.

The logging function with update-dhcp-status is best effort and not reliable, the journal is our Source of Truth and what we'll be relying on, for ease of developers and log viewers, we'll also add best effort version for now.
Just use `$SECONDS` here and everywhere. It will give you seconds since the script started. You technically don't even need an original start time since this will always be 0 here.

Are we sure we are reporting useful info with these messages. Isn't the parser on the other side going to look for success to show the state is done? How does it differentiate intermediate messages vs the end of the state? This transitions from SUCCESS to FAIL potentially.
Adjusted and right now we're reporting just "ongoing" state as other end need to implement theirs and its not on timeline.
This should be combined with the message above, but you need to do it on this line.
Acknowledged - changed code accordingly to take off legacy messages.
Maybe you should split setting the IP and hostname for your logic?
Probably you could do an elapsed time on the setting logic since it does a dbus call.
This is before any hooks are run, so it's probably in the wrong spot. Nothing in this script is firmware related.
Don't make the tmpdir here, keep it in the upgrade logic

Total time of the whole process?

nit: Why `ntboot_com` and not `netboot_com`, surely it's already a decent number of characters
This should be made into a separate change, it has nothing to do with changing the message values
You could drop `json` from the name as it's irrelevant to the caller and just an implementation detail. Plus it makes the call lines shorter.

Maybe it would be easier if this function had a dictionary of states and then handled the time itself? You could have a roughly

```
# declare outside function
declare -A NETBOOT_STATUS_START=()

if [[ $code == START ]]; then
  NETBOOT_STATUS_START=$SECONDS
fi

time=$((SECONDS-NETBOOT_STATUS_START["$state"]))
```
I think you got rid of the wrong thing, we are missing the state file output
Don't update any of the messaging state before lock acquisition. Do this after the traps below
You can delete this now that we have the json outputting the same thing
You can delete this now that we have the json outputting the same thing
I was thinking `dhcp_ip` because it's under `dhcp` state. If you prefer `start_ip_set` it can be odd how about `dhcp_ip_set`? Not sure, let me know what you think.
Let me know if you don't like my naming convention now.

Just calculate time inline, no need to subshell

`update_netboot_status_json "dhcp_ip" "$((SECONDS-start_set_ip))" "Setting ip ${ipv6}" "SUCCESS"`

IIRC you can drop the extra dollarsign on SECONDS
Why -5? Isn't -1 usually typical for errors?
I don't see why this 3rd message gets added, it doesn't give any info or have an intermediate step before it.
I would dump all the DHCP info in this message (ipv6, hostname, bootfile url) or just drop it since they get printed later.
Let's dump better to so we can see everything easily.
Can we just move this state into the if statement? It doesn't make sense if the fqdn is empty and it doesn't actually do anything.
You can drop `BR` from the text. Also get rid of elapsed since it's built-in now.
You can drop this, the `update_netboot_status` will give us the output
